assumptions: That the flag rollout caused the failures is inferred from timing in the service logs alone. The flag provider's own history reported zero recent changes, so either that feed is incomplete or the flag state was changed by some path it does not record.

No production change was found in any window queried, so the possibility that the buggy code shipped in an unrecorded deploy was raised but never ruled in or out. The competing 'latent bug shipped earlier' explanation remains untested rather than refuted.

The incident is recorded as ended at 14:30:28, but no mitigation was applied and the last log line read (14:29) still showed a 32% error rate. Whether the condition genuinely cleared, or the flag was turned off by someone outside this workflow, or the alert simply stopped firing, is not established.

The investigator repeatedly placed the incident start at 14:21, two to three minutes before the first ZeroDivisionError appears in the logs. The 14:21-14:22 errors are baseline upstream timeouts, so the true onset is taken here to be 14:23.
The blast radius is assumed to be limited to account-page requests because that is the only endpoint named in the logs; no other endpoint or downstream consumer was examined.
The proposed fix in the draft pull request has not been reviewed, tested, or verified to resolve the error.
input.executive_summary: Between roughly 14:23 and 14:30 UTC on 17 September 2026, a customer-facing shop service began failing requests to the account page. Roughly a third of account-page requests failed each minute at the peak; measured across the alert window, 21.5% of traffic failed that otherwise would not have. Customers hitting their account page in that window would have seen an error instead of the page; other parts of the shop were unaffected, and no data was lost or corrupted. The automated responder investigated three times and consistently identified the same trigger — a newly switched-on feature that contained a division-by-zero bug on the account page — but it could not confirm that trigger through the feature-management system, which reported no recent changes, and it therefore had no safe, reversible action to take. It took no action at all during the incident. Errors stopped being reported after 14:30; the reason for the recovery is not established by the evidence collected, and it was not the result of anything the responder did. The responder then opened a draft code change proposing a fix for the underlying bug and escalated the incident to a human owner, where it remains open.
input.root_cause: Enabling the `monthly-spend-feature` flag on io-shop exposed an unguarded division in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:32`, so account-page requests that reached the newly live code path raised ZeroDivisionError; application logs show the flag at 10/200 evaluations at 14:23 and fully on from 14:24, and the per-minute account-page error rate moving from a ~0-3% baseline (UpstreamTimeout noise) to 29-36% over exactly those minutes. This is a correlation drawn from the service's own logs only: the flag provider's change history returned zero recent changes, no deploy was recorded in any window queried (24h, ~62h, and 13:00-14:30Z), and no rollback or flag flip was ever performed, so the causal link was never confirmed by reversing it.
